draft.shortGloss: to repair; to fix; to correct
draft.emotion: competent and focused, taking care of a job that needs attention
notes: Form IV verb; the present tense is يُصْلِحُ (yuṣliḥu) and the verbal noun is إِصْلَاح (iṣlāḥ).
With بَيْنَ (bayna, 'between'), it means to reconcile or make peace between people.
Do not confuse with رَتَّبَ (rattaba, 'to tidy up, organize'); أَصْلَحَ means restoring something broken or wrong.

senses.definition: To make something that is broken or damaged work again.
To correct, improve, or set right a mistake, situation, or relationship.

examples.translation: He tried to correct his mistake.
examples.emotion: earnest and humble, wanting to make things right

draftBefore.shortGloss: to repair; to fix; to correct
draftBefore.emotion: competent and focused, taking care of a job that needs attention
notes: Use أَصْلَحَ when you want to say you are fixing a broken object or repairing a situation. It is the standard verb for 'repair' or 'mend'.
Do not confuse this with رَتَّبَ (rattaba), which means to tidy up or organize, whereas أَصْلَحَ implies that something was malfunctioning or damaged and is now being returned to working order.
